values.note: 15 paved single-family sites; 'Will accept trailers/RV's up to 50''. recreation.gov's catalog rates most sites 40-60 ft (one 75, one 25), three pull-through; site 2 is a walk-to site for bicyclists. Gravel road in, paved campground and spurs.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/indian-trees-campground ('This paved campground has 15 sites', 'Will accept trailers/RV's up to 50'', 'Site #2 is designated for use by bicyclists') + recreation.gov campsite catalog for 233882 (Max Vehicle Length, Driveway Entry 'Pull-through' on 3) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233882 ('Road to campground is gravel, but the campground and parking spurs are paved'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Potable water May-September (peak season). Garbage service and a camp host; food storage required.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/indian-trees-campground ('picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, garbage service, potable water and camp host', 'Potable water is available (May - September) in the campground during peak season.', 'Food storage required'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 'Peak season is Memorial Day through Labor Day. Non-peak season is dependent upon weather, but historically the campground will open early May and close end of September.'

Forest Service-run (Darby-Sula Ranger District). Some sites reservable on recreation.gov on a 6-month rolling window, until 4 days before arrival; the rest are first-come, first-served, and all are walk-up from the day after Labor Day to the end of September. 16 consecutive days, then move 5 miles. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/bitterroot/recreation/indian-trees-campground ('Some sites can be reserved through www.recreation.gov. Individual sites at this campground operate on a 6-month rolling basis.', 'Other sites are first come/first served', 'Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days. After 16 days, you must move 5 miles away') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233882 (rules reservationCutOff 4 days, maxConsecutiveStay 16) + /rates (2026 Walk-Up Season 09-08 to 09-30), read 2026-10-22

note: Bitterroot NF campground 3/4 mi off US-93 at the bottom of Lost Trail Pass, ~6 mi south of Sula, 5,128 ft; named for the nearby groves of cambium-peeled ponderosa pines (Bitterroot Salish cultural sites, do not damage the bark). Lost Trail Hot Springs under half a mile away; Nez Perce NHT trail starts near the turnoff. --Claude
summary: Confirmed $15 (2026; fees left as recorded), no hookups, 15 paved sites, 50-ft limit, vault toilets/potable water, some sites reservable on recreation.gov and the rest first-come. Changed season closes 09-07 -> 09-30 (the FS says it historically closes end of September; 09-07 was the end of the reservable season). Added pull-throughs, 6-month window, 16-night limit. Note trimmed of restated values.
